To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of tags to profile users improves the quality of recommendation in a social recommendation system.

(a) a tripartite nearest neighbor algorithm that uses tag, resource and resource vector of tag information to compute user similarity is better than using only one type of information; and (b) the resource nearest neighbor algorithm is better than the tag nearest neighbor algorithm.

(i) tag-based collaborative filtering algorithms can improve the quality of resource recommendation and (ii) the combination of three views of data (tags, resources and the collection of tag for a resource) can further improve the quality of recommendation
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of algorithms that use both tags and resource metadata for resource recommendation.
the development of a novel resource recommendation algorithm that combines both resource and tag information.
the problem of recommending resources to users based solely on tags and resource-interest knowledge, without requiring users to rate the resources they are familiar with.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed algorithm, TRNNA, provides better quality of recommendations than the other three algorithms.
our approach to using tags in collaborative filtering algorithms to recommend resources to users is effective and provides high-quality recommendations.
the proposed algorithms are capable of providing better recommendations than the baseline algorithms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TRNNA is a better algorithm for recommending resources than TNNA, RNNA and RVTA.
the combination of tags and resources provides better recommendation than either alone.
TRNNA is the best of all the algorithms we tested.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of resource and tag knowledge is necessary to provide high quality recommendation to users.
the combination of tag and resource knowledge can improve the quality of collaborative filtering recommendations.
a combination of different views can provide a better recommendation of resources to users than using any of these views individually.
